newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse must move on after crisis.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse must move on after crisis.

text.p: The Athens bourse has made strides forward but its main challenges, improved infrastructure and more efficient surveillance, remain problems, stock exchange president Manolis Xanthakis said on Tuesday.

"Infrastructure improvement and enhanced market surveillance are the two basic problems as regards the modernisation of the exchange," he told a conference on the modernisation of Greece's capital market.
"Both of these areas remain untackled fully since 1994," he told the conference sponsored by the Union of Hellenic Banks and the American Hellenic Chamber of Commerce.
The stock exchange plans to bring Greece's active bond market, now traded over the counter, to the bourse next year and render it more standardised and transparent, he said.

"In cooperation with the Madrid stock exchange we have set up a platform to trade bonds. This should start next year and banks who now trade these instruments over the counter will be participants," Xanthakis said.
The recent crisis sparked by the Delta Securities scandal in early November came at a time when the lack of efficient market surveillance allowed brokers to engage in illegal trading activities.
It was a shock for the market. But it could be turned into a positive development, Xanthakis said.

He said that despite recent problems, the bourse "is not the market we all knew a few years ago," underlining the exchange's satisfactory liquidity as compared with the competing Istanbul stock exchange.
"Intraday trading volume in Athens is about 10 percent of the total daily volume compared to about 90 percent in Istanbul," he said.
